lower_bound.quote: We use the following elementary infinite sunflower fact: every infinite family of distinct finite sets has an infinite subfamily $X_{i_1},X_{i_2},\ldots$ for which there is a fixed set $R$ satisfying
lower_bound.witness: Counterexample: let $X_n=\{1,2,\ldots,n\}$. These are distinct finite sets. In any infinite subfamily, choose indices $i<j<k$. Then $X_i\cap X_j=X_i$, whereas $X_j\cap X_k=X_j$, and $X_i\ne X_j$. Hence no fixed $R$ can equal every pairwise intersection. The asserted unbounded infinite-sunflower fact is false.
lower_bound.load_bearing: This false fact is the sole justification of Lemma 1. Lemma 1 is then used to prove that terminal members, their union $P$, and ultimately the family $\mathcal C$ are finite.

parsed.notes: The support characterization and periodicity assembly are valid. The finiteness argument fails because it invokes a false sunflower statement for finite sets of unbounded cardinality.
